solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stew fruit for Spooner’s classically trained actor (8)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner’s: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase is a spoonerism

blocks.note: stew = COOK, fruit = MELON; swap the opening sounds of COOK MELON

annotation.surface: A recipe note about stewing fruit, oddly tied to a stage actor.
annotation.walkthrough: The swap is approximate: MOOK KELLON only roughly matches how the name is said.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sir Ian McKellen trained in Shakespeare and classical theatre long before playing Gandalf.

entries.clue: Lose machine pistol, unfortunately abandoning hit on rogue (8)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: what is left of the pistol comes out badly arranged
indicatorNotes.abandoning: the pistol's letters give up the named group
indicatorNotes.rogue: HIT ON goes astray, so its letters appear in a different order

blocks.note: these five letters are removed, in the order they sit in MACHINE PISTOL
what remains after HIN and TO go, ready to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone loses a gun, having given up on a hit against a crook.
annotation.walkthrough: Two rearrangements stack here: the letters of HIT ON are taken out of MACHINE PISTOL, and the eight survivors are then rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lose your keys is to put them somewhere you cannot find.

entries.clue: Furore over contracts (5)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, turned over means read upwards

blocks.note: to cause a stink = to kick up a furore

annotation.surface: An uproar about some contracts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun about deals, but it is a verb, as brows do when a person frowns.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: brows that knit draw together, so knitting is a kind of contracting.

entries.clue: Exposed figure in trouble climbing coastal region (7)

indicatorNotes.Exposed: a figure stripped of its outer letters
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing means read from the bottom up

blocks.note: to ail = to trouble; AIL upwards is LIA, split round the figure

annotation.surface: A nude statue stuck in trouble on a coastal climb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' suggests nakedness, but here it means peeled: FIGURE loses its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Liguria is the strip of Italian coast around Genoa.

entries.clue: Head of college dropped for real (4)

indicatorNotes.dropped: in a down clue, the top letter drops to the bottom

blocks.note: a tech is a technical college; TECH less its head
the T at the top of TECH moves to the foot

annotation.surface: A college principal genuinely demoted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of college' reads as a principal; it is only the first letter of the college, which falls to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from German, where echt means genuine, used in English for authentic things.

entries.clue: Whacked and remains in bunk (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the remains go inside the bunk

blocks.note: a bunk is a BED; its first letter, before the remains
ash is what remains after burning

annotation.surface: Someone beaten and lying dead in a bunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' suggests a body; it is what is left after a fire.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are informal past tenses for striking something hard.

entries.clue: Opposite some army, not natives retreating (7)

indicatorNotes.some: only part of the following words is used

annotation.surface: Facing part of an army of foreign troops in retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: The military picture of an army retreating hides a word for 'opposite' read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: in grammar an opposite is a word meaning the reverse of another, like hot for cold.

entries.clue: With post in support, present other side (9)

indicatorNotes.in support: in a down clue, the post sits beneath and holds up the other part

blocks.note: present = here, as at a roll call

annotation.surface: A job applicant holding a post while showing their other side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' is the Latin prefix for after, not a job or a fence.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'the other side' is a euphemism for life after death, which is what the word names.

entries.clue: One moving quickly turned down that woman (6)

indicatorNotes.turned: the word for down is turned back to front

annotation.surface: A quick mover who rejected a particular woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned down' reads as rejected; split it into 'turned' as the instruction and 'down' as the mood.
annotation.definitionFit: An agent noun: someone who dashes is moving quickly, as Santa's reindeer Dasher does.

entries.clue: Weapon left in grass ruined (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the L goes inside the word for grass

blocks.note: to grass (inform on someone) = to SING, split round the L

annotation.surface: A weapon left lying in the grass, now spoilt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for informing to the police, so it is a verb, not the lawn.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a slingshot, or catapult, is a simple hand weapon for flinging stones.

entries.clue: Teaching in France, you tinker with course, ultimately getting demoted (8)

indicatorNotes.in France: the word for you is the French one
indicatorNotes.getting demoted: in a down clue, the letter moves lower down the entry

blocks.note: a TOERAG is a scoundrel or tramp, as a tinker was; its E is pulled out
the E, last letter of coursE, drops to the bottom

annotation.surface: A French pupil fiddling with their course and being moved down a class.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' is the noun, an old insult for a travelling mender, like the British toerag, not the verb fiddle.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal noun: tutorage is the work or office of a tutor, so teaching.

entries.clue: Picked up car parts – exhausts (5)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear: heard

blocks.note: tyres, British spelling of the rubber on car wheels

annotation.surface: Someone collects car parts, including exhaust pipes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhausts' looks like car parts too, but it is the verb: wears out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long walk tires or exhausts you.

entries.clue: Desire tips from actor Charlie Sheen (6)

indicatorNotes.tips from: the tips here are the final letters

annotation.surface: An actor's desires, with the name Charlie Sheen as the punchline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Actor Charlie Sheen' is a single famous name, but the definition is only the surname.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: polished wood has a soft shine, a sheen.

entries.clue: Primitive prudent to muffle sound (5-3)

indicatorNotes.to muffle: the word for prudent wraps round the sound, as a muffler wraps round a noise

blocks.note: sage = wise, prudent; split after its first letter

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned person careful to keep the noise down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primitive' reads as a noun for a person, but the answer is an adjective, hence the hyphen.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: anything crude or outdated is called stone-age, after the era of stone tools.

entries.clue: Propose moving radioactive waste once mutated wisteria removed (8)

indicatorNotes.moving: the remaining letters shift into a new order
indicatorNotes.removed: the wisteria letters are taken out
indicatorNotes.once mutated: WISTERIA's letters are in a different order in the waste, as if it had been changed earlier

blocks.note: these eight letters are taken out
the eight letters left, ready to rearrange

annotation.surface: A campaigner proposing to shift nuclear waste after it mutated a garden plant.
annotation.walkthrough: The removed letters are an anagram of WISTERIA, hence 'once mutated'; the survivors are then rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to argue publicly for a plan is to put it forward, to propose it.

entries.clue: Bid in good time for computer application (7,6)

annotation.surface: An auction bid lodged in good time for some software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bid' suggests an auction; it is the old verb meaning order, as in 'do as you are bid'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Windows program where users type text instructions goes by this name.

entries.clue: Interdependence of lifting corporation with excellence leader overlooked (9)

indicatorNotes.lifting: in a down clue, the word is read upwards
indicatorNotes.leader overlooked: the first letter is left out

blocks.note: a corporation is jokingly a pot belly, a TUM, read upwards

annotation.surface: Business jargon about a rising corporation depending on excellence under a neglectful boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old slang for a large belly, so the business picture is a decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a relationship of mutual dependence is one where each side relies on the other.

entries.clue: Backing old American in China pursuing contract rivals (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the old American goes inside the word for china
indicatorNotes.pursuing: this part comes after the bridge players

blocks.note: in contract bridge, East and South are opponents
china = mate, from rhyming slang china plate; PAL split round the American

annotation.surface: Support for an old American in China who is chasing rival firms for a deal.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang gives china plate = mate. Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, and E and S are on opposing sides.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: to espouse a cause is to back it, and the noun is that support.

entries.clue: Ways of hiding nauseous reaction being imprisoned by two deities (13)

indicatorNotes.hiding: OF holds the reaction inside it
indicatorNotes.being imprisoned by: the result is locked between the two gods

blocks.note: OF from the clue, split round the reaction

annotation.surface: Methods of concealing queasiness while locked up by a pair of gods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word joining 'Ways' to the rest, but it is wordplay material.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a main road is a public way, and roads are often called ways in street names.

entries.clue: The devil among us? (2,5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'the devil' works as an intensifier in a question, not as a noun

blocks.note: the emphatic phrase in 'what the devil is going on?'
here in the world of the living

annotation.surface: A suggestion that Satan walks among ordinary people.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: 'the devil' is not Satan but the phrase that adds force to 'what the devil?', which can be swapped for 'what on earth?'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an intensifier in questions, and a phrase for being in this world among the living.

entries.clue: Using every effort, disregard entertaining act on vacation (4,3)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: the word for disregard hosts the other part
indicatorNotes.on vacation: act is vacated, emptied of its middle

blocks.note: to flout a rule = to disregard it; FLOUT split round the act

annotation.surface: Working all out while ignoring a holiday entertainer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' suggests a holiday; here it means emptied, keeping only the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: working flat out means at full speed, with every effort.

entries.clue: A time to wear gym shoes, according to some, changes (6)

indicatorNotes.to wear: the time is worn inside the shoes

blocks.note: daps is a regional word for plimsolls; DAPS split before its last letter

annotation.surface: Some people claim a certain time demands gym shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'According to some' flags a regional word: in Wales and the West of England, plimsolls (canvas gym shoes) are daps.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to adjust something for a new use is to alter it.

entries.clue: Drug chart reviewed following one entering stupor (8)

indicatorNotes.reviewed: the chart is looked at again from the other end
indicatorNotes.following: the chart comes after the rest
indicatorNotes.entering: one goes into the word for stupor

blocks.note: a DAZE is a stupor, split round the one
a MAP is a chart, reviewed

annotation.surface: A drug chart checked after a patient falls into a stupor.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue names the chart first, but 'following' puts it at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: diazepam, sold as Valium, is a sedative drug.

entries.clue: Tailless monkey covers metres to get to grass (6)

indicatorNotes.Tailless: the monkey loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.covers: the shortened monkey wraps round the M

blocks.note: a BABOON is a monkey; lose the N and split round the metres

annotation.surface: A monkey without a tail stretching metres to reach the grass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' sounds like a lawn, but botanically the giant woody plant belongs to the grass family, so the definition is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A botanical fact: this tall woody plant is a member of the grass family.

entries.clue: Be niggled regularly lacking shade (5)

blocks.note: nIgGlEd, keeping the second, fourth and sixth letters

annotation.surface: Irritated by always being in the sun without shade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be' is used as it stands, and 'regularly lacking' keeps the alternate letters of 'niggled'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this pale sandy colour is one shade among many.

entries.clue: Writer of superb I, Robot (4)

indicatorNotes.of: the answer is made of part of the following words

annotation.surface: An author of the superb novel I, Robot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at Isaac Asimov; the writer is a thing that writes, and Biro is the British name for a ballpoint.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a pen is literally a writer, and in Britain any ballpoint is called by this brand name.

entries.clue: Told nosey parker earlier (5)

indicatorNotes.Told: spoken, so the answer is heard

blocks.note: a pryer is one who pries into other people's business

annotation.surface: Someone warned a busybody ahead of time.
annotation.walkthrough: A nosey parker is British slang for a busybody.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prior engagement is one arranged earlier than this one.

entries.clue: Models I twice separately encountered in record books (9)

indicatorNotes.encountered in: each I is met inside a part of the record books

blocks.note: tomes are large books; TOMES split round the second I

annotation.surface: Supermodels appearing twice in the record books.
annotation.walkthrough: The usual plural drops the second I, and the paper later apologised for the spelling; the wordplay still builds this form.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a perfect example of a type serves as a model of it.

entries.clue: Bladed tool hurt – article put aside for year (6)

indicatorNotes.put aside for: one letter is set aside and another takes its place

blocks.note: to scathe = to harm; SCATHE with its A (article) set aside
the article A, which is taken out of SCATHE
Y = year, in place of the A

annotation.surface: A blade that did harm, with a newspaper piece shelved for a year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing; it is the grammatical article A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the long curved mowing blade on a pole is a classic bladed tool.

entries.clue: Nut clamping to wheel oddly in vehicle recess (8)

indicatorNotes.clamping: the nut grips the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a nut is a FOOL, split round the wheel letters

annotation.surface: A loose nut tightened onto a wheel in a car's recess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a bolt fitting in a car picture, but it is a person, a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A compound: the recess in a car's floor is the well where the driver's feet go.
